PHYSICIAN EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This Physician Employment Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of October 1, 2026 (the "Effective Date") by and between Cascade Valley Medical Group, P.C., a Washington professional service corporation (the "Group"), and Naomi K. Osterhout, M.D., an individual (the "Physician").

RECITALS

A. The Group operates a multi-specialty medical practice in Spokane County, Washington, and is affiliated with Cascade Valley Hospital.

B. The Group wishes to employ the Physician as a board-certified gastroenterologist, and the Physician wishes to accept that employment, on the terms set out below.

1. Employment and Duties.

The Group employs the Physician as a full-time gastroenterologist. The Physician shall provide professional medical services to patients of the Group, shall maintain an average of thirty-two (32) clinical hours per week over each quarter, and shall participate in the Group's call rotation on an equitable basis with other gastroenterologists. The Physician shall devote substantially all professional time to the Group and shall not engage in outside clinical practice without the Group's prior written consent, which the Group shall not unreasonably withhold for academic appointments, expert witness work, or unpaid volunteer service.

2. Professional Independence.

Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to permit the Group to control, direct, or interfere with the Physician's exercise of independent medical judgment in the care of any patient. The Physician retains sole responsibility for all clinical decisions and shall practice in accordance with the applicable standard of care, the medical staff bylaws of any facility at which the Physician holds privileges, and the ethical standards of the profession.

3. Licensure, Privileges, and Credentialing.

The Physician shall maintain at all times: (a) an unrestricted license to practice medicine in the State of Washington; (b) a valid DEA registration; (c) board certification in gastroenterology by the American Board of Internal Medicine; (d) active medical staff membership and clinical privileges in good standing at Cascade Valley Hospital; and (e) participation in good standing in Medicare, Medicaid, and each commercial payer network in which the Group participates. The Physician shall notify the Group in writing within three (3) business days after any of the following: the suspension, restriction, or revocation of any of the foregoing; the commencement of any professional-liability claim, disciplinary proceeding, or governmental investigation involving the Physician; or any event that would make the Physician an Excluded Individual.

4. Compensation.

4.1 Base Salary. The Group shall pay the Physician an annual base salary of $525,000, payable in accordance with the Group's regular payroll practices and subject to lawful withholding.

4.2 Productivity Compensation. In addition to the base salary, the Group shall pay the Physician productivity compensation equal to $58.00 for each work relative value unit ("wRVU") personally performed by the Physician in a calendar year in excess of 6,800 wRVUs, computed under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule in effect on the Effective Date. The Group shall calculate productivity compensation within forty-five (45) days after the end of each calendar year and pay it within thirty (30) days after the calculation.

4.3 Fair Market Value; No Referral-Based Compensation. The parties intend that all compensation under this Agreement is consistent with fair market value for the services actually provided, is commercially reasonable, and does not take into account, directly or indirectly, the volume or value of any referrals or other business generated by the Physician for the Group or any affiliate. Compensation is set in advance for the term and does not vary with referrals. The parties intend that this Agreement satisfy the bona fide employment relationship exception under 42 U.S.C. Section 1395nn(e)(2) and the employee safe harbor under 42 C.F.R. Section 1001.952(i).

4.4 Benefits. The Physician is eligible for the Group's health, dental, disability, and retirement plans on the same terms as other employed physicians, and for reimbursement of up to $8,000 per year of documented continuing medical education, licensure, DEA, and professional-society expenses, plus twenty (20) days of paid time off and five (5) days of continuing-education leave per year.

5. Professional Liability Insurance.

The Group shall obtain and maintain professional liability insurance covering the Physician with limits of not less than $1,000,000 per claim and $3,000,000 in the annual aggregate. If the policy is written on a claims-made basis, the Group shall purchase an extended reporting endorsement ("tail") covering the Physician for claims arising from services rendered during the term, at the Group's expense, except that if the Physician terminates without Good Reason before the third anniversary of the Effective Date, the Physician shall bear one-half of the cost of the tail.

6. Term and Termination.

6.1 Term. The initial term is three (3) years from the Effective Date and renews automatically for successive one-year terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least one hundred twenty (120) days before the end of the then-current term.

6.2 Termination Without Cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement without cause on one hundred eighty (180) days' written notice.

6.3 Termination by the Group for Cause. The Group may terminate immediately on written notice if the Physician: (a) loses or has restricted the license, DEA registration, board certification, privileges, or payer participation required by Section 3; (b) becomes an Excluded Individual; (c) is convicted of a felony or of any crime involving fraud, dishonesty, or moral turpitude; (d) fails to maintain professional liability coverage; or (e) materially breaches this Agreement and does not cure the breach within thirty (30) days after written notice describing it.

6.4 Termination by the Physician for Good Reason. The Physician may terminate for Good Reason on sixty (60) days' written notice if the Group materially reduces the base salary, materially diminishes the Physician's duties, or relocates the Physician's principal practice site more than thirty-five (35) miles, and in each case the Group does not cure within thirty (30) days after the Physician's written notice.

6.5 Effect of Termination. On termination the Physician shall complete the medical records of patients seen through the termination date, cooperate in the orderly transition of patient care, and return all Group property. The Group shall pay all earned but unpaid base salary and any productivity compensation earned through the termination date, prorated, within thirty (30) days after termination.

7. Patient Records and Continuity of Care.

All patient medical records are and remain the property of the Group, subject to each patient's rights under applicable law. Neither party shall interfere with a patient's choice of physician. On termination, the Group shall notify the Physician's patients of the Physician's departure in a manner consistent with Washington law and the ethical obligations of both parties, and shall provide the Physician a list of the patients the Physician treated in the preceding eighteen (18) months for the sole purpose of notifying them of the Physician's new practice location.

8. Confidentiality and HIPAA.

The Physician shall keep confidential all patient information and the Group's business information, shall use protected health information only as permitted by the Group's policies and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and its implementing regulations, and shall complete the Group's privacy and security training annually. This obligation survives termination indefinitely as to protected health information and for three (3) years as to other confidential business information.

9. Restrictive Covenants.

9.1 Non-Competition. For twelve (12) months after termination, the Physician shall not provide gastroenterology services at any facility located within fifteen (15) miles of the Group's principal office at 720 East Sharp Avenue, Spokane, Washington. This restriction does not apply if the Group terminates without cause or the Physician terminates for Good Reason, and it does not apply to services provided at Cascade Valley Hospital in an emergency.

9.2 Non-Solicitation of Employees. For twelve (12) months after termination, the Physician shall not solicit for employment any employee of the Group with whom the Physician worked, other than through a general advertisement not targeted at Group employees.

9.3 No Restriction on Patient Choice. Nothing in this Section restricts a patient's right to choose the Physician as a treating physician, and nothing prohibits the Physician from providing continuing care to a patient who seeks it.

9.4 Enforcement. The parties agree the restrictions in this Section are reasonable in duration and geography and necessary to protect the Group's legitimate business interests. If a court finds any restriction unenforceable, the court shall reduce it to the maximum enforceable scope rather than strike it.

10. Indemnification.

The Group shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Physician from any claim arising out of the Physician's provision of professional services within the scope of employment, except to the extent the claim arises from the Physician's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or criminal act. The Physician shall give the Group prompt written notice of any such claim, shall permit the Group to control the defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Physician, and shall cooperate at the Group's expense. The Group shall not settle any claim requiring a report to the National Practitioner Data Bank without the Physician's prior written consent.

11. Dispute Resolution.

The parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute by good-faith discussion between the Physician and the Group's president within thirty (30) days after written notice of the dispute. A dispute not resolved that way shall be submitted to binding arbitration before a single arbitrator in Spokane County, Washington, administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Employment Arbitration Rules. The arbitrator may award any relief a court could award, and either party may seek injunctive relief in court to enforce Section 9.

12. General.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Washington, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. It is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties. It may not be assigned by the Physician; the Group may assign it to a successor to its practice. If any provision is unenforceable, the remainder remains in effect. It may be executed in counterparts.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

CASCADE VALLEY MEDICAL GROUP, P.C.
